title: Dynamic MCP Install — IndexEntry.launch + built-in catalog + register_mcp_server
description: Make the agent capable of installing MCP servers end-to-end. Today install_mcp_server writes only description/install_url to .mcp.json — no command/args/env — so installs are unusable bookmarks. Three stories: (US-001) extend IndexEntry with launch and propagate through marketplace + installer + cache; (US-002) seed a small built-in catalog so discover_capability returns hits without external registry; (US-003) add register_mcp_server LLM tool for direct/external installs the agent can trigger from a README description. Constraint: no command allowlist (user explicitly skipped), no chrome-devtools-mcp hardcoding as a special case — chrome-devtools just happens to be one of the catalog seeds.

stories.title: Plumbing: IndexEntry.launch + installer writes command/args/env
stories.description: Extend IndexEntry with optional launch dict, parse it in marketplace coercion, write it through install_mcp_server into .mcp.json. Discovery cache round-trips the field automatically via dataclasses.asdict / IndexEntry(**data); add a regression test. Refuse MCP installs that lack launch info (writing a launchless entry produces a useless bookmark).

stories.title: Built-in MCP catalog seeds discover_capability without external registry
stories.description: Add a small static catalog (3 entries: chrome-devtools, filesystem, fetch) inside marketplace.py. fetch_mcp_candidates returns built-in matches alongside (or instead of) network results. This makes discover_capability functional out of the box without mcp_registry_url being configured.

stories.title: register_mcp_server LLM tool for direct installs from user-supplied launch info
stories.description: Add a new LLM tool the agent can call when the user describes an MCP from a README. Tool takes slug, description, command, args, env?, source_url? and constructs an IndexEntry on the fly, then calls install_mcp_server. Same consent gate, same .mcp.json write, same restart prompt. The agent must read back the proposed config before treating user_confirmed=true as valid (this is a prompt-engineering rule in the tool description, not a code-side check).
